title: All 36 selected fits give smaller row-centroid amplitudes after pointing subtraction for KIC 8462852
abstract: We test the known 0.88-day signal near KIC 8462852 in three selected Kepler release 25 intervals. All 36 fits give a smaller row-centroid half-amplitude after subtraction of the archived pointing estimate. The primary reductions are 86.7%, 73.3% and 73.5% in quarters 8, 9 and 16. The tests change the polynomial baseline width and the trial frequency. Paired residual-block tests support a reduction in quarter 8, but remain inconclusive in quarters 9 and 16. The quarter 16 column amplitude increases. A shared pointing or aperture contribution can explain the row result. Removal of real source signal by the correction is also possible. The result does not locate the source or reproduce earlier detector-wide cleaning. We find no new planet or signal. Independent instrument confirmation is absent. The bundle contains code, aggregate tables, figures, exact input hashes and a separate-scratch retrieval recipe.

display.caption: Row-centroid amplitudes fall after unit pointing subtraction in the selected fits. Thin bars show conditional noise-perturbation ranges; they remain wide.
